skill.name: ghe-design
skill.description: Guidance for writing domain-specific requirements documents with clear purpose, references, and testable acceptance criteria.
skill.summary: Helps AI agents draft clear, verifiable requirements for varied technical domains.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: Most static command and network findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline paths, and reference links. The audit confirms the ~/.claude write allowance and flags absolute prompt-control wording plus mandatory full-report posting.

remediation.suggestion: Remove ~/.claude from allowed write locations or require explicit user confirmation for each settings change.
Replace absolute language with guidance that respects system, safety, and repository instructions.
Make external posting opt-in and require user confirmation before sharing full reports outside local storage.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when requirements are vague or forced into one template. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create clear, testable requirements for each domain.
actual_capabilities: Defines core elements that every requirements document should include.
Provides domain patterns for algorithms, games, finance, distributed systems, and security.
Encourages clear acceptance criteria and external references.
Guides GHE report naming and report placement expectations.
Explains how to adapt structure to the problem domain.
limitations: Does not generate executable code or run validation tools.
Assumes the GHE agent workflow and role names.
Contains broad instructions that may not fit every repository policy.
Includes external references that users should verify before relying on them.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Requirement
use_cases.description: Create a concise requirement with purpose, acceptance criteria, assets, and references before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Specify a Technical System
use_cases.description: Document architecture, failure modes, data contracts, and verification steps for complex engineering work.

use_cases.title: Prepare Security Requirements
use_cases.description: Capture threat models, trust boundaries, mitigations, and security headers in a format engineers can verify.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-design to draft requirements for this feature: [feature]. Include what, why, acceptance criteria, and references.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt to a Domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-design to write requirements for [domain]. Choose sections that fit the domain and explain how completion will be verified.

prompt_templates.title: Expand an Existing Requirement
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to improve a draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-design to review this requirement draft: [draft]. Add missing constraints, edge cases, references, and testable acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cross-Discipline Specification
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complex system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-design to create a full requirement for [system]. Cover architecture, risks, compliance, failure modes, assets, and verification evidence.

output_examples.input: Request requirements for a dark mode toggle.
output_examples.output: A short requirement describing the toggle, user value, persistence behavior, system preference handling, transition expectations, and acceptance checks.

output_examples.input: Request requirements for a payment flow.
output_examples.output: A structured requirement covering compliance, transaction flow, retention rules, audit logging, failure handling, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Request requirements for an authentication system.
output_examples.output: A security-focused requirement with threat model, trust boundaries, authentication flow, required headers, and measurable controls.

best_practices: Start with the user goal, then add only sections that improve clarity.
Make every acceptance criterion observable and testable.
List external references without copying large source documents.
anti_patterns: Do not force every requirement into the same template.
Do not replace user requirements with silent improvements.
Do not use vague success terms without verification evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create requirements documents that describe what to build, why it matters, and how to verify completion.

faq.question: Is this a fixed requirements template?
faq.answer: No. It presents patterns and required basics, while allowing the structure to match the domain.

faq.question: Which domains does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes examples for algorithms, games, finance, distributed systems, security, and simple product features.

faq.question: Can it help with acceptance criteria?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes measurable acceptance criteria so implementers can prove the requirement is complete.

faq.question: Does it run commands or generate code?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance text for requirements writing and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: What should users review before installation?
faq.answer: Users should review the broad agent instructions, the ~/.claude write allowance, and the GitHub report posting rule.
